text: AgentTeams 是面向 DeepSeek Harness 的多智能体团队协作插件，适合需要把复杂目标拆解并交给多个角色并行推进的开发、研究和审查工作。它将团队生命周期工具接入 Harness，并可通过自然语言或 /agent-teams 启动；用户可先检查成员名单和任务依赖，再批准计划运行。成员作为可持续的子代理按依赖领取任务，通过团队消息交付进展，队长汇总结果。Web 界面提供团队活动面板、计划编辑器和对话中的团队卡片，展示任务状态并可打开成员会话。可配置成员模型、角色、任务策略及本地状态目录；不要求额外 API key，运行依赖 Harness 的 subagent 服务。

AgentTeams coordinates durable subagents in DeepSeek Harness. Users can stage a roster and dependency graph, review and approve it, then track ready tasks and member reports in the Web activity panel. Members can use configured model routes and exchange team messages.
我想把一个复杂开发目标拆成几个有依赖关系的任务，交给不同角色并行处理。
能不能先让我检查团队计划和成员分工，确认后再开始执行？
我需要多个子代理协作完成研究任务，并把各自进展发回给负责人。
想查看当前团队有哪些任务、每项由谁负责以及依赖是否完成。
让 DSH 根据我的目标组织一组不同模型或角色的代理来做代码审查。
我想从聊天里启动团队任务，并在网页侧栏跟踪完成进度。
I want several role-based agents to work on a goal with task dependencies and send progress back to a captain.
Can I review a team plan in the Web interface and approve it before any member starts work?
AgentTeams 的功能「计划审阅」：创建时可将成员名单和任务依赖图保存为待审计划；用户批准后才启动成员和调度任务。
AgentTeams 的功能「依赖调度」：队列根据任务依赖和成员空闲状态分派已就绪任务，成员领取后更新执行状态。
AgentTeams 的功能「团队消息」：成员可通过团队消息向队长或队友汇报任务进展，消息会进入收件箱并在后续步骤提供。
AgentTeams 的功能「Web 活动面板」：侧栏读取团队快照，展示成员与任务活动，并从界面打开成员会话。
AgentTeams 的功能「命令启动」：聊天命令 /agent-teams 接收目标，也支持配置 profile；命令输入会作为用户消息进入对话。
AgentTeams 使用前须知：团队状态默认写入当前工作区的 .agent-teams 目录；可通过 stateDir 更改位置。
AgentTeams 使用前须知：启动团队成员需要 Harness 中有可用的 subagent provider；默认配置使用 spawn provider。

@nanmicoder/dsh-agent-teams README · One prompt. A working team.：`dsh-agent-teams` turns the current DeepSeek Harness session into a captain that can assemble durable sub-agents, split a goal into dependency-aware tasks, and coordinate work through direct messages.

Ask in natural language. The plugin provides the team protocol, 14 coordination tools, persistent state, an automatic shared-task scheduler, and a live Web UI—without requiring a separate workflow engine.

@nanmicoder/dsh-agent-teams README · Releases：[Latest release](https://github.com/NanmiCoder/dsh-agent-teams/releases/latest) restores member model fallback on Harness `0.2.2-rc.1` and improves task settlement, activity updates, and artifact auditing. The recommended host is Harness `0.2.1-rc.2`. See the [tested matrix](./compatibility.json) and [release notes](./release-notes/v0.1.29.md).

@nanmicoder/dsh-agent-teams README · Why AgentTeams?：| Capability | What it changes |
| --- | --- |
| **Captain-led delegation** | The current session creates the team, assigns roles, and consolidates the final result. |
| **Durable members** | Members are continuable DSH sub-agents that can be woken for focused follow-up turns. |
| **Dependency-aware tasks** | Tasks move through explicit states and cannot be claimed before their dependencies finish. |
| **Automatic reuse and safe takeover** | Idle members claim the next ready task; reassignment revokes stale attempts before new work starts, and cold recovery retries stranded open attempts. |
| **Direct messaging** | Members send durable mailbox messages directly to teammates or the captain—no relay required. |
| **Live activity panel** | The Web UI combines segmented progress, a collapsible roster, and an interactive task DAG; running tasks show the member's model, and completed archives retain their full member and task history. |
| **Plan before execution** | Normal `/agent-teams` runs stage an unspawned roster and DAG first. The Web panel uses the host model catalog for member routes. Returning to chat stops the planning turn,

@nanmicoder/dsh-agent-teams README · Why AgentTeams?：The conversation card and activity panel use Harness's official locale service. They follow live language changes between English and Simplified Chinese—including status labels, dynamic summaries, controls, archive markers, and accessibility text—without a page reload or a separate plugin setting.

@nanmicoder/dsh-agent-teams README · Install and choose versions：CI verifies the exact hosts listed above the last row. The installer accepts other hosts at or above the minimum version.

@nanmicoder/dsh-agent-teams README · Desktop app：In the app sidebar, open **Plugins → Add plugin**. You can install directly from GitHub by pasting this repository URL into the plugin input, without a version, tag, or commit suffix:

```text
https://github.com/NanmiCoder/dsh-agent-teams
```

This installs from the default branch and is available immediately after release. The equivalent shorthand is also supported:

```text
github:NanmiCoder/dsh-agent-teams
```

@nanmicoder/dsh-agent-teams README · Desktop app：For npm installation, enter the versioned spec `@nanmicoder/dsh-agent-teams@0.1.29`. Desktop's pnpm 11 defaults to a 24-hour minimum release age: for 24 hours after a release, a bare package name or `@latest` installs the previous version even when the preview shows the newest one, and the installation fails if that version is incompatible with your host. An exact version installs immediately. Changing registry mirrors does not remove this policy. GitHub access is required for the Git route; it may contain newer code than npm.

@nanmicoder/dsh-agent-teams README · Desktop app：Install it, then choose **Enable now**. If the host asks for a restart, restart the desktop app. Do not disable compatibility checks or the global release-age policy to install the plugin.

@nanmicoder/dsh-agent-teams README · Desktop app：The desktop app supplies its own Harness core and package manager. Upgrading the global CLI does not upgrade that core, and an ordinary standalone CLI cannot manage its desktop profile. The CLI carrier installed by the desktop app can manage that profile in `0.2.1-rc.2`. Check the embedded core against the compatibility list. Harness `0.2.1-rc.2` is now the exact published target; its RC status is unchanged. The earlier source-only `0.2.0` prediction is no longer a support declaration. See the [release migration evidence](./docs/harness-0.2.1-rc.2/README.md).

@nanmicoder/dsh-agent-teams README · CLI / Web: 1. Install DeepSeek Harness：```sh
npm install --global @deepseek-ai/dsh
dsh --version
```

The command selects the host's npm `latest`; check `dsh --version` against the support matrix after upgrading. Alpha is opt-in: select an exact Alpha version from the table and lock all host dependencies as described in the [maintenance guide](./docs/maintenance-workflow.md).

@nanmicoder/dsh-agent-teams README · CLI / Web: 2. Install the AgentTeams plugin：Install or upgrade from npm with an exact version (currently `0.1.29`):

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add --save-exact @nanmicoder/dsh-agent-teams@0.1.29
```

For a CLI-managed installation, replace `web` with your active CLI profile. **Stop and restart that profile's Harness process, then refresh the browser.** Installing the plugin does not upgrade Harness; the host and plugin have independent `latest` channels.

text: @nanmicoder/dsh-agent-teams README · View teams in the workspace：Click **View team** in the current chat header or the team card below a reply to open the native **Team collaboration** tab. The entry belongs to its chat, rather than the general workspace start page.

@nanmicoder/dsh-agent-teams README · View teams in the workspace：Team and task content starts immediately: wide panes use columns and narrow panes stack them. Select a task to locate its owner; member icons open their conversations. Closing the tab does not stop the team, and its chat can reopen it. Completed teams retain their archives. Older hosts keep the activity panel.

@nanmicoder/dsh-agent-teams README · How it works：1. For a request to use AgentTeams, the captain follows the core protocol already in its system instructions. It continues an existing team and uses `agent_teams_status` when current state needs checking. When no team exists, the goal becomes a staged plan for review.
2. The captain adds role-specific members backed by continuable sub-agents.
3. The goal becomes tasks with owners and explicit dependencies.
4. The shared scheduler uses real `running / idle / ready` state to atomically claim one ready task per idle member and wake it. An interrupted resident attempt stays parked and can resume through a direct message without losing its capability; after a cold process restart, the scheduler retries stranded open work with a fresh attempt.
5. Members update with the current `attempt_id`; reassignment or captain takeover revokes the old attempt and waits for the old worker to quiesce before a new attempt starts.
6. The captain presents the combined result, then archives the complete team record.
@nanmicoder/dsh-agent-teams README · How it works：Team state is stored under `<workspace>/.agent-teams/`; the Web panel reads that disk truth and combines it with live sub-agent activity.

@nanmicoder/dsh-agent-teams README · How it works：Member creation is zero-interaction by default: a member on the captain's current LLM route snapshots that provider, model, and reasoning effort, while a member on a requested alternative route snapshots the target model's default effort; later continuations restore the resolved snapshot. Only an explicit heterogeneous-team request (for example, “backend on provider A/model X, frontend on provider B/model Y”) supplies a member-specific `provider` + `model`; there is no per-member model or reasoning prompt.

@nanmicoder/dsh-agent-teams README · How it works：Captain sessions keep the concise core protocol and the original 14 native team tools from their first request. All business tools are directly available; no loading tool or extra activation call is needed. Configured profiles retain their bounded directory in the fixed system prompt. Creating, approving, continuing or ending a team does not rewrite the system prompt or tool schemas. Core rules remain available after history compaction or discarded code-mode tool results. Members receive four team tools, fixed member instructions, and their ordinary coding/research tools. Web approval wakes the captain with a control message; later member reports wake it again. See the [fixed protocol and benchmark contract](./docs/progressive-loading.md).

@nanmicoder/dsh-agent-teams README · Slash command：No “use AgentTeams” phrasing required. The plugin registers the
closed-namespace `/agent-teams` host command, so the Web GUI slash menu shows
an `agent-teams` placeholder with an input hint: pick it (or type the
command), describe the goal, and press Enter.

```
/agent-teams research the pricing pages of three competitors
```

@nanmicoder/dsh-agent-teams README · Slash command：The command pipeline claims the line, then preserves that exact input as an
ordinary user follow-up so it remains visible in the main chat. The gesture
boundary adds the deterministic activation directive at pre-step, so the
first model request follows the staged planning protocol without a mandatory helper call. The invocation is also durably
logged (`command/run` / `command/done`).

@nanmicoder/dsh-agent-teams README · Slash command：Surfaces without command adjudication (for example the headless CLI) get the
same deterministic activation through a gesture boundary: any genuine user
message starting with `/agent-teams` activates the protocol for the rest of
the text. Mid-sentence mentions stay ordinary prose.

Historical panels require saved team state or archives. Sessions from early versions that deleted teams without retaining archives do not yet support reconstructing the full panel from logs.

@nanmicoder/dsh-agent-teams README · Configuration：Defaults work without extra setup. A trusted profile can override member behavior:

```yaml
- id: agent-teams
  config:
    stateDir: .agent-teams
    memberProvider: spawn

@nanmicoder/dsh-agent-teams README · Configuration：`memberMaxDepth` defaults to `0`: team members cannot create nested subagents. Set `1` to explicitly permit one descendant level; the limit also covers runtime/code-tool calls. Default members report through team messages only, avoiding duplicate native parent reports. Idle roster members make no model requests. Task assignments start distinct turns; coordination joins the nearest model step. Acceptance and consumption are tracked separately. Removal/archive drains the selected branch and its pending input before reporting success.

@nanmicoder/dsh-agent-teams README · Configuration：`toolPolicies` is owner configuration: reusable per-member tool policies keyed by id. A member *selects* one by id — `tool_policy` on `agent_teams_add_member`, a member row of an inline `plan`, or a profile member row. The Captain model can select a declared policy but can never submit raw allow/deny lists or invent one at runtime.

@nanmicoder/dsh-agent-teams README · Configuration：- `deny` hides the named global tools from that member's schemas and rejects their invocation.
- `allow` keeps only the named global tools. The four coordination tools (`agent_teams_claim_task`, `agent_teams_update_task`, `agent_teams_send_message`, `agent_teams_status`) are always added to an allow list.
- The captain-only tool list is always denied and cannot be reopened by a policy; a policy may not deny a required coordination tool.
- Unknown ids, empty policies, and empty lists fail at mount or before a member is persisted.
- `agent_teams_status` shows the selected policy id per member; the complete resolved filter is kept in `team.json` for audit, and the child's durable descriptor reapplies it after a restart.
- Teams and members created without a policy keep their previous tool set and record shape. An empty `tool_policy` on `agent_teams_edit_plan` clears a staged member's policy.
@nanmicoder/dsh-agent-teams README · Configuration：This is model tool visibility and invocation policy for global tools, not an OS sandbox or an authorization boundary.

@nanmicoder/dsh-agent-teams README · Configuration：`memberProvider` is the sub-agent runtime backend (`spawn` / `fork`), not an LLM provider. Cross-LLM-provider routing uses the optional `provider` + `model` fields of `agent_teams_add_member`; `memberModel` is only a model default for all members. A member on the captain's current provider/model inherits the captain's reasoning effort, while a changed provider or model automatically uses the target model's default. To request a particular effort, pass the optional `reasoning_effort` field — one of the target model's supported effort ids, or `"default"` to force the model's own default.

@nanmicoder/dsh-agent-teams README · Configuration：`slashCommand: false` disables the deterministic `/agent-teams` activation surfaces (slash command and gesture boundary), leaving the natural-language trigger as the only entry point.

@nanmicoder/dsh-agent-teams README · Boundaries：- One captain leads one active team at a time.
- Idle members with no open task are automatically reused for ready work. An idle member that still owns an open attempt is parked until messaged or explicitly reassigned; messages that cannot be delivered live remain durable and are retried at a later status boundary.
- State is file-backed and serialized within one DSH process; concurrent processes editing the same team are not coordinated.
- The activity panel reports persisted state as-is. Models may occasionally finish work without performing the expected task-state update.
@nanmicoder/dsh-agent-teams README · Boundaries：See [docs/usage.md](./docs/usage.md) for the full tool reference, state model, Web UI behavior, configuration, and known limits.

@nanmicoder/dsh-agent-teams README · Plugin development Skill：Community upgrade, audit, benchmark, testing and release skills are vendored with a pinned source revision. See [skills/README.md](./skills/README.md) for local rules and [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md) for the contribution workflow.

@nanmicoder/dsh-agent-teams README · Named multi-role profiles：Configure one or more complete team profiles in `cordis.patch.yml`. A profile always supplies the roster (independent provider/model/role/reasoning effort). Set `taskPlanning: captain` when the Captain should derive the DAG from the user's goal; omit it or set `taskPlanning: seed` to keep a fixed template workflow:

```yaml
profiles:
  demo-delivery:
    description: Ship a small feature
    protocol: Discuss requirements, review, test, then prepare release; do not deploy automatically.

@nanmicoder/dsh-agent-teams README · Named multi-role profiles：Use an explicit profile flag: `/agent-teams --profile demo-delivery implement the feature`. The first ordinary token is never treated as an implicit profile. Normal command runs call `agent_teams_create({ profile, approval: "required" })`: the roster and seed/Captain-designed DAG remain staged, no child session is created, and no task is claimed. Edit the plan in the activity panel using the host model catalog, return to chat so the Captain asks what to revise and then atomically updates the same draft, discard it, or click **Approve & Run**. Return/discard actions cancel any planning turn still running; discard also parks model-facing context that forbids silently creating a replacement team. Approval resolves the final provider/model/reasoning choices, commits the roster, and creates each member session only when its first task is ready. A running team is stopped from its own panel header through a confirmation dialog rather than from the composer. Direct tool clients may pass `approval: "automatic"` for the legacy immediate path. Failed review/test tasks do not unlock downstream work; automatic repair/review tasks do
